gen-eater-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-next: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next has lowercase eyes as big as washers. Eater does the dark, wide-spaced menace with short ascenders, while the sans does the quiet job of keeping its hooked rounds unsealed and easy to tell apart.
gen-eater-gf-fresca: Dark and aggressive, Eater swells gently along its curves and spaces its letters wide apart. Fresca stays ruler-straight in weight, with counters that open out to the surrounding space.
gen-eater-gf-funnel-sans: Dark and aggressive, Eater sets the tone with wide-spaced letters. Funnel Sans keeps its strokes steady as a fixed pen, so the heavier curves above get an orderly partner below.
gen-eater-gf-gafata: Eater spaces its letters wide and keeps its ascenders stubby. Gafata sets a tall band of wide-eyed lowercase with short stalks above, so running text moves along smoothly.
gen-eater-gf-georama: Eater brings dark, widely spaced letters with moderate stroke swelling. Georama keeps capitals barely rising and its c pulled open, so the plain sans leaves all the attitude to Eater.
gen-eater-gf-golos-text: Eater has sturdy hairlines and wide gaps between its letters. Golos Text draws true monoline sans letters, with a widely parted s and lowercase that fills the line, steadying the heading.
gen-eater-gf-hind-mysuru: Hind Mysuru reads smooth and unfussy, its lowercase tops pressing close to ascender height. But Eater, with a calm gradient of weight along its rounds, supplies the dark edge.
gen-eater-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara keeps one thickness in every direction, with spacious gaps in rounded letters. And Eater shifts weight noticeably yet never dramatically, so the dark heading stays readable.
gen-eater-gf-huninn: Huninn reads plainly, with bowls that rise close to cap height and no thinning at the sides. While Eater handles menace through slightly lighter hairlines, Huninn handles the quiet, uniform lettering.
gen-eater-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight reads like bent tubing, smooth with no swelling. Eater keeps its thin strokes sturdy and spaced wide, which gives the sans-serif text below a firm, dark partner.
